key_insight: Increasing spanwise convex curvature delays hypersonic boundary-layer transition by weakening centrifugal amplification while preserving the dominant Görtler–sinuous breakdown pathway.
engineering_relevance: Spanwise curvature offers a potential geometry-based lever for delaying transition and managing surface heating in hypersonic designs.
method: Direct numerical simulation and Mach 7 experiments.
Smooth doubly curved surfaces with fixed streamwise concavity and increasing spanwise convex curvature.
Spectral proper orthogonal decomposition to identify dominant disturbance dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations and experiments show consistent trends in transition location, thermal-streak organisation and disturbance evolution, with greater spanwise curvature delaying breakdown.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify transition-delay magnitude or establish applicability beyond the tested geometries and flow conditions.
paper_title: Effects of Spanwise Curvature on Hypersonic Boundary Layer Transition in Görtler-driven Flows
